radar.title: Sweden eases mining permits to cut China minerals reliance
radar.excerpt: Sweden has declared the mining of critical minerals and rare earths a national security interest. This will ease and expedite the permit process. The government said the step was needed to counter dependence on China.

radar.title: ECB keeps interest rates unchanged amid Iran war inflation
radar.excerpt: The European Central Bank has kept its base interest rates steady but said it was "closely monitoring" the energy price shock. The impact of the war against Iran on energy costs has pushed inflation over ECB targets.

radar.title: Canada-EU: Closer trade ties to counter Trump?
radar.excerpt: Given they share the world's longest land border, Canada and the US have historically enjoyed fruitful trade relations. But with Donald Trump escalating his tariff war, Canada is looking to the EU and further afield.

radar.title: EU fines Google €890 million over competition rules
radar.excerpt: The European Commission said it found that Google had preferenced its search engine and app store in ways that unfairly harmed competition.

radar.title: Who is Ukraine's new military chief?
radar.excerpt: Mykhailo Drapatyi has been made commander-in-chief of Ukraine's armed forces. His appointment follows a cabinet reshuffle that ousted defense minister Fedorov.

radar.title: Russia's businesses under strain from Ukraine's attacks on Wildberries
radar.excerpt: Ukrainian drones have hit several retail warehouses belonging to Russia's biggest online retailer Wildberries in a matter of days.

radar.title: Hungary: Ex-PM Orban pledges resistance to Magyar 'tyranny'
radar.excerpt: Hungary's former prime minister alleges that his successor has "dismantled the rule of law and eliminated checks and balances." Peter Magyar has pursued Viktor Orban and his allies since winning April's elections.

radar.title: How Russia is luring foreign nationals to fight in Ukraine
radar.excerpt: More and more, Russia is recruiting men from the world’s poorest countries to send them to the front in the Ukraine war. Why are people joining up?

radar.title: Turkey-PKK talks: Is peace finally possible?
radar.excerpt: A year ago, the Kurdish militant group PKK announced an end to its armed struggle. Since then, peace talks with Turkey have progressed slowly, but some observers believe they could succeed.

radar.title: AliExpress hit with record EU fine
radar.excerpt: The Chinese retailer has become the latest major online marketplace to face penalties under the EU’s Digital Services Act.

radar.title: Sixteen titles in five years - why Spain are a dominant force
radar.excerpt: We look at what's behind Spain's dominance after they become the first nation to be men's and women's World Cup champions at the same time.

radar.title: Victory for football? Spain beat Argentina to win World Cup
radar.excerpt: It might seem like a trite cliche, but you won't find many neutrals disagreeing with that verdict on the World Cup final.

radar.title: ‘Everyone's afraid to die’: Struggle to recruit soldiers in Ukraine turns violent
radar.excerpt: Aggression against recruitment officers has become increasingly threatening, police say.
